filings.ratePer100.national.unit: eviction filings per 100 renter households per year

source.title: Estimating Eviction Prevalence across the United States (Gromis, Fellows, Hendrickson, Edmonds, Leung, Porton, Desmond; PNAS 2022)

spread.basis: 95% credible interval of 2018 modeled filings / renting_hh; year-to-year range 2010-2018 is 7.80-9.40

filings.ratePer100.national.notes: Derived: filings_estimate 3,656,428 / renting_hh 46,902,048 x 100. 2010-2018 average 8.68 (derived). Modeled 'comprehensive' estimate (court + proprietary data, imputed where missing). The raw proprietary national file (us_proprietary_2000_2018.csv, observed-only coverage) shows 4.61 for 2018; do not use it as a rate because coverage is incomplete. Households threatened (filings net of serial refilings) 2018: 2,734,663 = 5.83 per 100 (derived).

filings.ratePer100.byState.unit: eviction filings per 100 renter households per year (median of 50 states + DC)

source.title: Estimating Eviction Prevalence across the United States (Gromis, Fellows, Hendrickson, Edmonds, Leung, Porton, Desmond; PNAS 2022)

spread.basis: range across states in 2018 (SD lowest, MD highest); 10th-90th percentile 1.50-15.89

filings.ratePer100.byState.notes: Derived per state: filings_estimate / renting_hh x 100. byState = 2018; byStateAvg2010_2018 = mean of the nine annual rates (derived). Per-state 95% CI bounds are in byStateLow2018/byStateHigh2018. Maryland's very high rate reflects heavy serial filing there and is real in the data. No Eviction Lab state estimates exist for PR, GU, VI, AS, MP: use the national value with a wide spread there (gap, not a measured number). Value field is the median state, not a renter-weighted average.

arrears.shareBehind.unit: share of adults in rent-paying renter households not currently caught up on rent

source.title: Household Pulse Survey, Phase 4.2 Cycle 09 (Aug 20 - Sep 16, 2024), Housing Table 1b: Last Month's Payment Status for Renter-Occupied Housing Units

spread.basis: approx. 95% interval from the table's standard error (448,256 on 9,442,445 'No')

arrears.shareBehind.notes: Derived: 9,442,445 'No' / (56,084,424 'Yes' + 9,442,445 'No') = 14.4%; excludes occupied-without-rent and non-reporters (14.3% if non-reporters on the caught-up question are kept in the denominator). Unit is adults 18+, not households, and the survey is experimental. Cycle 09 is the last Household Pulse cycle (survey ended Sept 2024). Housing Table 3b, same cycle: of those behind who reported, 16.7% were less than 1 month behind, 40.5% 1 month, 22.9% 2 months, 19.9% 3+ months (derived from counts); median is 1 month behind.

arrears.monthsAtFiling.unit: months of rent owed when the eviction is filed (typical)

source.title: Humphries, Nelson, Nguyen, van Dijk, Waldinger, 'Nonpayment and Eviction in the Rental Housing Market', NBER Working Paper 33155 (Nov 2024, rev. June 2025), Figure 1(b) 'Months Behind at Eviction Filing'
source.data: landlord ledger data, ~6,000 tenants, 2015-2019, low-income Midwest neighborhoods, 56% Chicago

spread.basis: Eviction Lab claim-amount court records: Harris County TX median claim about 1 month of median rent in Jan-Mar 2020; New York City pre-pandemic median claim just under 2x median rent, about 3x by late 2020 (claims include fees and damages)

arrears.monthsAtFiling.notes: The paper states 'landlords usually wait until a tenant owes two or more months of rent before filing' and '90% of evicted tenants owe at least one month of rent'; the histogram mode is 2 months. The value 2 is that stated typical point, not a published median. The same paper estimates filing costs landlords the equivalent of 2-3 months of rent. Philadelphia (Eviction Lab) median claim about $2,000 early 2020, above $4,500 after 2022, in dollars, not converted to months.

source.title: Estimating Eviction Prevalence across the United States (Gromis, Fellows, Hendrickson, Edmonds, Leung, Porton, Desmond; PNAS 2022)

spread.basis: Boston Housing Court 2014 final judgments for landlord ~32% (Dixon et al. 2016, cited in Urban Institute 2023 'Masking the Scarlet E'); Milwaukee County Dec 2019: writ in 42.2% of 1,101 filings (AASEW study); Pennsylvania excl. Philadelphia: judgment for landlord 80% pre-pandemic, 73% in 2023 (Housing Alliance of PA from AOPC data; share of outcomes, likely includes judgments by agreement)

outcomes.judgmentShare.notes: Derived: 779,069 judgments / 2,003,340 filings in the observed proprietary records, 2018; 2010-2018 average 0.398, falling from 0.424 (2010). Ratio taken within the same observed records, so incomplete coverage cancels; judgments are not recorded everywhere, so treat as approximate. A judgment can be by default or agreement and does not always mean a completed lockout.

outcomes.settledOrDismissedShare.unit: share of filings dismissed, withdrawn or resolved by stipulation without a judgment for the landlord

source.title: Comprehensive Study of Evictions Filed in Milwaukee County, Wisconsin (Phase 1), Executive Summary, Dec 2019 filings

spread.basis: low: Pennsylvania excl. Philadelphia pre-pandemic, 1 - 0.80 landlord judgments (Housing Alliance of PA; withdrawn alone rose 7% to 14%, 2018-2023); high: national complement of Eviction Lab judgment ratio, 1 - 0.389 (derived, includes pending/other outcomes)

outcomes.settledOrDismissedShare.notes: Milwaukee: 559 of 1,101 cases (50.8%) dismissed by stipulation, at the plaintiff's request, or by judgment; trade-group study, one month, one county. Many stipulations still require the tenant to leave (159 of 525 agreements had a move-out date). No national settled/dismissed series was found; treat as estimated.
